en.h: A 2,628-acre park at the confluence of the Mississippi and Wisconsin rivers, just south of Prairie du Chien, established in 1917 as Wisconsin's fourth state park. Wyalusing means 'home of the warrior' in Lenape, the language of the Munsee-Delaware who settled here in the 19th century. Its mounds archaeological district is on the National Register.
en.ff: 500-foot bluffs dotted with prehistoric Native American mounds overlook the valleys; the Wyalusing Hardwood Forest is a National Natural Landmark. It lies in the unglaciated Driftless Area.

en.r: Kinnickinnic State Park is a state park in Wisconsin, United States. It covers 5.5 km² and has been protected since 1972. It is managed by the state government.
en.h: A 503 ha Wisconsin state park where the Kinnickinnic River, known locally as the Kinni, joins the St. Croix River. The mouth of the Kinnickinnic forms a sandy delta where boaters can picnic and camp.
en.ff: The banks of the Kinnickinnic are lined with eastern white pine, and the river is rich in trout. More than 140 bird species pass through the valley during migration; bald eagles appear in winter. Wild turkeys were reintroduced in 1989. Mammals include white-tailed deer, raccoons, minks, foxes and beavers.

en.h: A 244-acre park in the Wisconsin Dells region, established in 1932 to protect sandstone walls and ledges.
en.ff: 500-million-year-old Cambrian sandstone carved by a former channel of the Wisconsin River, which now runs 1.5 miles east, leaving the gorge walls exposed.
at: Loop trail along the rock ledges

es.ff: Arenisca del Cámbrico, de 500 millones de años, tallada por un antiguo cauce del río Wisconsin, que hoy corre 2,4 km al este y dejó a la vista las paredes del cañón.

pt.r: O Wildcat Mountain State Park é um parque estadual em Wisconsin, nos Estados Unidos. Tem 15,2 km² e está protegido desde 1948, sob gestão do governo estadual.

at: Mirantes de Wildcat Mountain e Mount Pisgah

en.r: Wildcat Mountain State Park is a state park in Wisconsin, United States. It covers 15.2 km² and has been protected since 1948. It is managed by the state government.
en.h: A 3,643-acre park on the Kickapoo River in Wisconsin's Driftless Area, near Ontario, adjoining the Kickapoo Valley Reserve. Limestone-capped sandstone bluffs such as Wildcat Mountain and Mount Pisgah overlook the narrow valley. Human traces date back to 2000 BCE.
at: Wildcat Mountain and Mount Pisgah viewpoints

en.r: Wisconsin Islands Wilderness is a wilderness area in Wisconsin, United States. Under the IUCN system it is a wilderness area: a large, largely unmodified space without permanent infrastructure.
en.h: A 29-acre wilderness in Door County, Wisconsin, one of the smallest in the US: three uninhabited Lake Michigan islands (Spider, Hog and Gravel), managed by the Fish and Wildlife Service. A migratory bird preserve since about 1913; wilderness since 1970.
en.ff: A breeding ground for migratory birds.

en.r: Wade House Historic Site is a protected area in Wisconsin, United States. It covers 19 hectares and has been protected since 1953.

en.r: Porcupine Lake Wilderness is a wilderness area in Wisconsin, United States. It covers 17.4 km² and has been protected since 1984. It is managed by the U.S. Forest Service. Under the IUCN system it is a wilderness area: a large, largely unmodified space without permanent infrastructure.
en.h: An 18 km² wilderness in Bayfield County, Wisconsin, within Chequamegon-Nicolet National Forest. Namesake Porcupine Lake covers 29 ha and is up to 10 m deep; there are over ten lakes in the area.
en.ff: Oak, maple, hemlock and white pine dominate. The lakes hold trout, bass and northern pike; deer, bears, foxes and loons frequent the area.

en.r: Rainbow Lake Wilderness is a wilderness area in Wisconsin, United States. It covers 29 km² and has been protected since 1975. It is managed by the U.S. Forest Service. Under the IUCN system it is a wilderness area: a large, largely unmodified space without permanent infrastructure.
en.h: A 29 km² wilderness area in the Chequamegon unit of Chequamegon-Nicolet National Forest, Bayfield County, northern Wisconsin. It holds Rainbow Lake, fifteen other lakes and nine ponds, many reached by old logging trails and rail grades.
en.ff: Heavily wooded with northern hardwoods, balsam fir, pine and paper birch, some of it considered old-growth.
